name: Times means lots of
rule: × means "lots of". 3 × 4 can mean 3 lots of 4 or 4 lots of 3. Both make 12.
trick: Say "lots of" out loud. 3 lots of 4 is 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

another.text: Imagine 3 plates with 4 strawberries on each plate. Count all the strawberries and you get 12. That is 3 × 4.

steps.say: The × sign means "lots of". So 3 × 4 means 3 lots of 4.

steps.ask: How do we write 3 lots of 4 as an adding sum?
steps.hint: 3 + 4 only has one 4 in it. We need three 4s.

questions.stem: Which adding sum is the same as 4 × 2?

name: The 2 times table
rule: Multiply by 2 means double it. Double means add the number to itself.
trick: 6 × 2 is 6 + 6 = 12. Every answer in the 2 times table is even: it ends in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8.

another.text: You have 2 hands. 3 children have 6 hands between them: 2, 4, 6. Counting hands is counting in 2s.

steps.say: × 2 means double. Double means add the number to itself.

steps.then: Every 2 times table answer is even. That is a handy check.
steps.hint: Numbers ending in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 are even.

questions.stem: Which number is in the 2 times table?
questions.why: 2 times table answers are even. 14 is even: 7 × 2 = 14.

name: The 5 times table
rule: The 5 times table counts in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Every answer ends in 5 or 0.
trick: Count in 5s and hold up a finger each time. 4 fingers: 5, 10, 15, 20. So 4 × 5 = 20.

examples.note: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. It ends in 5, so it looks right.

another.text: A clock counts in 5s. When the long hand points at 3, it is 15 minutes past. When it points at 6, it is half past: 30 minutes.

steps.say: 4 × 5 means 4 lots of 5. Count in 5s and hold up a finger each time.

steps.ask: Start counting in 5s. What comes after 5?
steps.hint: Counting in 5s jumps by 5 each time.

steps.say: 4 fingers, and we landed on 20. So 4 × 5 = 20. It ends in 0, so it passes the check.

questions.stem: Which number is in the 5 times table?
questions.why: 5 times table answers end in 5 or 0. 35 = 7 × 5.

name: The 10 times table
rule: When you multiply by 10, the digits move one place to the left. A 0 fills the empty ones place.
trick: 4 × 10: the 4 moves from the ones to the tens. 4 tens is 40.

examples.note: The 7 moves to the tens place. 7 tens is 70.
Both digits move one place left: 120.

another.text: Think of 10p coins. 3 ten-pence coins make 30p. 6 of them make 60p.

steps.say: Multiplying by 10 makes a number ten times bigger. The digits slide one place to the left.

steps.hint: Just one place to the left: from ones to tens.

steps.then: The 0 sits in the ones place to hold it.

steps.say: Check by counting in 10s six times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60.

questions.why: The 9 moves to the tens place: 9 tens is 90.

questions.stem: Which number is in the 10 times table?

name: Swap them round
rule: You can swap the numbers in a times calculation and the answer stays the same. 3 × 8 = 8 × 3.
trick: Pick the easier way round. Counting in 7s ten times is slow, but 7 lots of 10 is easy: 70.

examples.note: 5 lots of 3 is 15. 3 lots of 5 is 15 too.

another.text: Put biscuits in 2 rows of 5. Now walk round and look from the side: it is 5 rows of 2. Same biscuits, same number: 10.

steps.say: 10 × 3 can mean 10 lots of 3. Counting in 3s ten times is slow! Let's swap it round.

steps.ask: Swap the numbers round. 10 × 3 is the same as:
steps.hint: Swapping keeps the same two numbers and the × sign.

steps.say: Swapping means you only learn half the facts. Know 3 × 8 and you already know 8 × 3.

questions.why: Swapping the numbers keeps the answer the same: 4 × 6 = 24.

name: The 3 times table
trick: 3 lots is 2 lots and 1 more lot. For 3 × 6: double 6 is 12, then add one more 6: 18.

another.text: A tricycle has 3 wheels. 2 tricycles have 6 wheels. 3 tricycles have 9 wheels.

steps.say: 3 × 6 means 3 lots of 6. 3 lots is 2 lots and 1 more lot.

steps.ask: First do 2 lots of 6. Double 6 is:

steps.then: Check by counting in 3s six times: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18.

name: The 4 and 8 times tables
rule: × 4 means double and double again. × 8 means double three times.
trick: 7 × 4: double 7 is 14, double 14 is 28. For 7 × 8, double once more: 56.

another.text: You have 2 legs. A dog has 4 legs, double yours. A spider has 8 legs, double the dog's.
another.example:
You: 2 legs
Dog: 4 legs
Spider: 8 legs

steps.say: × 4 is double, then double again.

steps.then: And for 7 × 8, double one more time: 28 + 28 = 56.
steps.hint: 14 is only one double. × 4 needs two.

questions.why: 8 is double 4, so double the answer: 12 + 12 = 24.

name: The 6 times table
rule: 6 lots is 5 lots and 1 more lot. 7 × 6 is 35 + 7 = 42.
trick: Or double the 3s: 4 × 3 = 12, so 4 × 6 = 24.

another.text: An egg box holds 6 eggs in two rows of 3. So the 6s are just the 3s doubled: 4 boxes hold double 12, which is 24 eggs.

steps.say: A trick for 6s: do the 5s, then add one more lot.

steps.then: Check with doubling: 7 × 3 = 21, and double 21 is 42.

name: The 7 times table
rule: 7 lots is 5 lots and 2 lots. Work out both and add them.

another.text: A week has 7 days: 5 school days and 2 weekend days. 3 weeks is 15 school days and 6 weekend days: 21 days.

steps.say: 7 is 5 and 2. So 7 lots of 8 is 5 lots of 8 and 2 lots of 8.
So 7 × 8 = 56. A rhyme helps: 5, 6, 7, 8. 56 is 7 × 8!

questions.why: 7 lots is 5 lots and 2 lots, so add 2 × 4: 20 + 8 = 28.

name: The 9 times table
rule: 9 lots is 10 lots take away 1 lot. 9 × 6 is 60 − 6 = 54.
trick: Check it: up to 10 × 9, the digits of a 9s answer add up to 9. 54: 5 + 4 = 9.

another.text: Hold up 10 fingers. For 9 × 3, fold down your third finger. There are 2 fingers before it and 7 after it: 27.

steps.say: 9 is one less than 10. So 9 lots is 10 lots take away 1 lot.

steps.hint: The 6 moves to the tens place.

steps.ask: Check: do 5 and 4 add up to 9?

name: The 11 times table
rule: Up to 9 × 11, the answer is the number written twice. 4 × 11 = 44.
trick: For 10, 11 and 12, use 10 lots and 1 more lot: 12 × 11 = 120 + 12 = 132.

another.text: 11 looks like twins: 1 and 1. Multiply it by a number up to 9 and you get twins too: 3 × 11 = 33.

steps.say: Up to 9 × 11, write the number twice, like 7 × 11 = 77. 12 is too big for that trick, so use 10 lots and 1 more lot.

steps.hint: The digits of 12 move one place to the left.

steps.then: 10 lots and 1 more lot makes 11 lots.
steps.hint: Writing it twice only works up to 9.

questions.why: Up to 9, write the number twice: 77.
The digits of 11 move one place to the left: 110.

name: The 12 times table
rule: 12 lots is 10 lots and 2 lots. 4 × 12 = 40 + 8 = 48.
trick: Do the 10s (easy), then double the number, then add them.

another.text: A dozen eggs is 12: a row of 10 and 2 spare. 3 dozen is 3 rows of 10 and 3 lots of 2 spare: 30 + 6 = 36.

steps.say: 12 is 10 and 2. So 7 × 12 is 7 × 10 and 7 × 2.

steps.hint: The 7 moves to the tens place.

name: Times and divide are a family
sub: Use a times fact to divide
rule: Every times fact has two divide facts. 4 × 5 = 20, so 20 ÷ 5 = 4 and 20 ÷ 4 = 5.
trick: For 24 ÷ 6, ask: what times 6 makes 24? 4 × 6 = 24, so the answer is 4.

another.text: Three numbers live in one house: 2, 5 and 10. They can make four facts together.

steps.say: ÷ asks: how many 3s make 18? A times fact can tell us.

steps.ask: Which times fact has 3 and 18 in it?
steps.hint: We need the answer to be 18.
15 is 18 take away 3. Divide asks how many 3s.

steps.say: The same family also gives 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

name: Sharing equally
rule: ÷ can mean share out equally, so everyone gets the same. 12 ÷ 3 means share 12 between 3.
trick: Deal them out one at a time, like cards, until they are all gone. Or use a times fact: 4 × 3 = 12, so each gets 4.

examples.note: Share 15 stickers between 5 children: 3 each, because 3 × 5 = 15.

another.text: Share a pizza with 8 slices between 4 people. Everyone gets the same, so nobody grumbles: 2 slices each.

steps.say: Sharing equally means every friend gets the same number.

steps.ask: Give each friend 1 grape. How many grapes have you given out?
steps.hint: There are 4 friends, and each got 1.

steps.ask: Give each friend 1 more. How many grapes are left?
One more each. How many are left now?
So how many grapes does each friend get?
steps.hint: 4 is the number of friends. Count the rounds.

questions.stem: Share 6 apples equally between 2 children. How many each?
Share 20p equally between 5 friends. How much each?

name: Times table stories
sub: Spot the times or divide words
rule: Each, every, lots of and groups of mean times. Share equally, split into and how many groups mean divide.
trick: Draw it! A quick sketch of the plates, bags or legs shows whether you are making a big pile or sharing out.

another.text: If the story ends with one big pile, you are putting groups together: times. If it ends with lots of small piles, you are sharing out: divide.
another.example:
groups → one pile: ×
one pile → groups: ÷

walkthrough.board: A hen lays 2 eggs every day. How many eggs does she lay in 5 days?

steps.hint: Look for each, every or lots of.
5 days with 2 eggs each day is 5 lots of 2.

steps.say: Say the answer with its word: 10 eggs.

questions.stem: 4 children each have 3 pencils. How many pencils is that?
18 cakes are shared equally onto 2 plates. Which number sentence finds how many go on each plate?

name: How many groups?
rule: When a story tells you the total and how many are in each group, count up in that times table until you reach the total. The number of counts is the answer.
trick: Use your fingers: one finger for each count. 5, 10, 15, 20 is four fingers, so 20 ÷ 5 = 4.

examples.note: Count in 2s up to 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 pairs.

another.text: Packing eggs into boxes of 6 is the same thing. Keep filling boxes until the eggs run out, then count the boxes.

walkthrough.board: A tricycle has 3 wheels. Ben counts 12 wheels. How many tricycles are there?

steps.ask: What does the story tell us?
options: The total (12) and how many in each group (3)
steps.hint: We know all the wheels, and the wheels on one tricycle.

steps.say: Count up in 3s until you reach 12. Put up one finger each time.

steps.ask: How many numbers did you say?
So how many tricycles are there?
steps.hint: 12 is the number of wheels. Count the tricycles.

questions.stem: Eggs go in boxes of 10. How many boxes do 40 eggs fill?
A table has 4 legs. There are 20 legs. How many tables are there?
questions.why: Count in 4s: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. That is 5 tables, because 5 × 4 = 20.

name: The 8 times table
rule: × 8 means double, double and double again. 5 × 8: 5, 10, 20, 40.
trick: Already know the 4s? Just double the 4s answer once more. 6 × 4 = 24, so 6 × 8 = 48.

examples.note: Double 3 is 6, double 6 is 12, double 12 is 24.

another.text: An octopus has 8 arms. That is double a dog's 4 legs, and a dog has double your 2 legs. Each step is a double.

steps.say: × 8 is three doubles in a row. Start with the 6.

steps.hint: 24 is only two doubles. × 8 needs three.

name: Use a fact you know
sub: One more lot or one less lot
rule: Stuck on a fact? Start from a fact you know that is next door, then add or take away one lot.
trick: 8 × 7: you might know 7 × 7 = 49. 8 lots is one more 7: 49 + 7 = 56.

another.text: It is like climbing stairs. If you know you are on step 49, the next 7s step is just 7 more up: 56.

steps.say: 8 × 6 means 8 lots of 6. Do you know a fact next door to it?

steps.ask: Which fact is next door to 8 lots of 6?
steps.hint: Next door means one lot fewer: 7 lots of 6.

steps.ask: 8 lots is one more lot than 7 lots. So add one more:

steps.then: A fact you know plus one more lot.

questions.why: 7 lots is one more lot of 6: 36 + 6 = 42.
9 lots is one less lot of 9: 90 − 9 = 81.

name: Counting in 11s
rule: To count on in 11s, add 10 and then add 1 more. 11, 22, 33, 44 ... 99, 110, 121, 132.
trick: After 99 the twins stop. Keep going the same way: 99 + 10 = 109, then 1 more is 110.

another.text: Climb 11 stairs at a time: a big jump of 10, then one little hop.

steps.say: These numbers count in 11s. To find the next one, add 11.

steps.hint: The tens go up by one: 9 tens becomes 10 tens, with 9 ones left.

steps.say: So the next number is 110. That is 10 × 11.

name: Counting in 12s
trick: 12 is a dozen. A box of a dozen eggs is 12, two boxes are 24, three boxes are 36.

another.text: There are 12 months in a year. Each birthday adds 12 more months: 1 year is 12 months, 2 years is 24, 3 years is 36.
another.example:
1 year → 12 months
2 years → 24 months
3 years → 36 months

steps.say: These numbers count in 12s. To find the next one, add 12.

steps.hint: Add one ten: 4 tens becomes 5 tens.

steps.say: So the next number is 60. That is 5 × 12.

name: Dividing by 2
rule: Dividing by 2 means finding half. Half splits a number into two equal parts.
trick: Use your doubles backwards. Double 7 is 14, so half of 14 is 7.

examples.note: Double 8 is 16, so half of 16 is 8.
Half of 20 is 10 and half of 2 is 1. 10 + 1 = 11.

another.text: Two children share a bag of 10 sweets so it is fair. Each child gets half: 5.

steps.say: ÷ 2 means split it into two equal halves.

steps.ask: Check: is double 9 the same as 18?

questions.why: Double 6 is 12, so half of 12 is 6.
Double 10 is 20, so half of 20 is 10.

name: Dividing by 10
sub: The digits move one place back
rule: When you divide by 10, the digits move one place to the right. 60 ÷ 10: the 6 moves from the tens to the ones. The answer is 6.

examples.note: The digits slide one place right: 12.

another.text: Swap 40p for 10p coins. 40p is 4 coins of 10p.

steps.say: Dividing by 10 makes a number ten times smaller. The digits slide one place to the right.

steps.hint: One place to the right: from tens to ones.
80 is 90 take away 10. Divide asks how many 10s.
The 9 moves to the tens place.

name: Rows in a story
sub: Rows and how many in each
rule: When things are set out in rows with the same number in every row, multiply: number of rows × how many in each row.
trick: Draw dots: one line of dots for each row. 3 rows of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12.

another.text: Look at a box of chocolates. 3 rows with 5 in each row is 15 chocolates, and you can check by counting them.

walkthrough.board: Mia puts 4 rows of plants in her garden. There are 3 plants in each row. How many plants are there?

steps.ask: How many plants are in each row?

steps.hint: 4 rows with 3 in each is 4 lots of 3.

steps.then: Say it with its word: 12 plants.

questions.stem: A tray has 2 rows of buns with 5 buns in each row. How many buns?
There are 3 rows of chairs with 10 chairs in each row. How many chairs?

name: Money stories
rule: When each thing costs the same, multiply the price by how many you buy. p means pence.
trick: Keep the p on your answer. 4 lollies at 5p each is 4 × 5 = 20, so 20p.

another.text: At a cake sale every cake costs 5p. Buy 1 for 5p, 2 for 10p, 3 for 15p. Count in 5s for each cake.

walkthrough.board: A rubber costs 5p. Leo buys 4 rubbers. How much does he spend?

steps.ask: How much does one rubber cost?
How many rubbers does Leo buy?

steps.hint: 4 rubbers at 5p each is 4 lots of 5p.

questions.stem: A balloon costs 2p. How much do 7 balloons cost?
A pencil costs 10p. How much do 5 pencils cost?
